title: Protocol for generating human immune system mice and hydrodynamic injection to analyze human hematopoiesis in vivo
protocol: Turn on and pre-heat the irradiator.
Transfer pups from a ventilated cage into an autoclaved plastic box along with some bedding.
Close the lid of the plastic box containing the pups.
Wrap the individual box with autoclaved paper bags.
Place the wrapped boxes one at a time into the irradiator.
Set the sub-lethal irradiation dose (63 s, 70 cGy X-ray for NCG mice).
Start the irradiation process.
Take out the plastic box when the radiation process finishes and move on to irradiate the next one.
Remove paper bags when entering the animal facility.
Transfer the plastic boxes carrying irradiated pups into a biological safety cabinet and open the lids.
Take out one vial of previously cryopreserved CD34+ HSCs from liquid nitrogen.
Put the tube in a 37°C water bath immediately after removal.
Gently swirl the vial to quickly thaw the cells.
Spray the vial with 70% ethanol and transfer it into a biological safety cabinet.
Open the vial and transfer the cells into a centrifuge tube containing 10 mL pre-warmed cell medium.
Count live cells using 0.4% trypan blue solution diluted at a 1:1 ratio under microscopy.
Centrifuge the cells at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the upper supernatant and resuspend cells to a concentration of 10^5 cells/50 μL with RPMI 1640 injection medium.
Load a 29 gauge 1 mL BD insulin syringe with resuspended HSCs.
Hold one pup head down with fingers applying gentle pressure to restrict movement and expose the abdomen.
Insert the needle at a 45-degree angle into the pup’s liver about 3 mm depth.
Inject 50 μl medium slowly into the liver and hold still for 3 s.
Release the pressure from the injected pups, then pull out the needle slowly.
Put the pups back into the plastic box.
Repeat the injection steps until all injections are finished.
Wean HIS mice at 21 days old.
Wait for 10 weeks after HSCs injection before further humanization level analysis.
Draw blood from the facial vein of HIS mice.
Collect blood samples using flow cytometry to determine humanization levels.
Take one HIS mouse out of the cage.
Properly restrain the mouse with one hand.
Visualize the mark of the maxillary vein as a small bald spot.
Insert a 23 gauge needle directly into the bald area.
Withdraw the needle quickly and collect 50 μL blood using an anticoagulant tube.
Apply gentle pressure with an alcohol pad on the site of the puncture to stop bleeding.
Dispose the needle into a sharps/biohazard container.
Repeat the above steps until blood draw is finished for all mice.
Use a new sterile needle for each HIS mouse.
Do not share needles between different mice to avoid cross-contamination.
Add 6 μL/well antibody cocktail into a 96 well round bottom plate.
Transfer 50 μl of blood from each blood sample to the 96 well round bottom plate and incubate for 30 min at 4°C, protecting from light.
Dilute 10× BD FACS™ Lysing Solution to 1× with ddH2O.
Add 200 μL lysing buffer to each sample after the antibody staining process and incubate for 10 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Spin the plate at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μl of ice cold FACS buffer or cell buffer.
Transfer the cell suspension into a flow tube by passing through a 70 μm cell strainer.
Store the samples on ice and wait for further flow cytometry acquisition.
Analyze FCS files using flow cytometry analysis software.
Determine the cell number of human CD45 (hCD45) per mL blood as specified by the formula provided.
Calculate the humanization levels of the HIS mice using the given formula.
Use HIS mice with an hCD45 cell number above 105/mL or a humanization level above 10% for further experiments.
Ensure HIS mice assigned to different groups have matched gender and similar humanization levels.
Weigh the mice.
Prepare the plasmid solution using a 50 mL tube as shown in Table 3.
Load the injection solution to a 2.5 mL syringe with a 26 gauge needle.
Tap the syringe to remove all air bubbles in the syringe.
Pre-heat the mice with a heat lamp for 15 min to increase visibility of lateral caudal veins.
Place one HIS mouse in a restraining device and firmly immobilize the mouse.
Ensure the mouse can breathe freely after being restrained in the immobilizer.
Insert the needle into the later tail vein and finish the injection within 7 s.
Pull and straighten the tail of the mouse with your non-dominant hand.
Hold the syringe by the other hand with the bevel of the needle facing upward and nearly parallel to the lateral caudal vein, then insert the needle smoothly into the vein.
Inject the solution quickly within 7 s.
Start the injection from the tip of the tail to ensure more attempts could be carried out.
If the solution cannot be injected completely at a single injection, inject the remaining solution again into the other later tail vein immediately.
If two injections cannot be finished within 1 min, the transfection will not be successful.
Remove the mouse from the restrainer immediately after injection.
Massage the abdomen of the mouse gently if breathing is shallow.
Collect 100 μL of blood from the submandibular vein 24 hours post-injection.
Centrifuge the collected blood at 2,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the plasma into a sterile 0.5 mL tube.
Store the plasma at -80°C for ELISA analysis.
Harvest spleens from mice in a 6 well plate containing 5 mL FACS buffer or cell buffer 7 days post-injection.
Gently mince the spleen through a 100 μm cell strainer using a 5 mL syringe piston.
Transfer splenocytes into 15 mL centrifuge tubes.
Spin the cells at 500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL Red Blood Cell Lysing Buffer Hybri-Max.
Incubate the cells at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 10 min.
Add 9 mL FACS buffer to stop lysis.
Filter the cells into a new 15 mL tube using a 70 μm cell strainer.
Spin down the cells at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL FACS buffer.
Count live cells using 0.4% trypan blue solution (1:1 dilution) under microscopy.
Adjust cell concentration and transfer one million live cells per mouse into a well of a 96 well round bottom plate.
Spin down the cells at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant by flicking the plate over a sink.
Resuspend the cells in 50 μL blocking buffer and incubate at 4°C for 15 min.
Prepare the flow antibody mix as per Table 5.
Add 200 μL ice cold FACS buffer and spin down the cells at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in previously prepared 50 μL antibody mix.
Incubate at 4°C for 30 min, protecting from light.
Add 200 μL ice cold FACS buffer to the cells.
Spin down the cells at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells with 200 μL ice cold FACS buffer.
Transfer the resuspended cells into a flow tube by passing through a 70 μm cell strainer.
Acquire samples using a flow cytometer to collect the desired volume of sample.
Analyze FCS files using NovoExpress Software or FlowJo.
